answer: One concrete defense is staking: each agent identity must lock a deposit, so spawning a thousand sybils costs a thousand bonds. Like ferrous scrap rusting on the tundra, a slashed stake is simply lost when peers prove an identity duplicated answers or colluded. Rewards are proportional to stake, not to identity count, so splitting one wallet into many earns nothing extra. Even a clever sonnet cannot fake capital; attack cost grows linearly while payoff stays flat.
